chunks: The disciples gathered to Isa (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'O teacher of goodness, guide us aright.' So he said to them: 'Musa, the Prophet of God, ordered you that you should not swear by God as liars, and I order you that you should not swear by God, neither as liars nor as truthful ones.'

key_terms.الْحَوَارِيُّونَ: The hawariyyun — the close disciples of Prophet Isa (Jesus), equivalent to the apostles in Christian tradition
key_terms.الْيَمِين: Oath/swearing (implicit in تَحْلِفُوا) — the act of invoking God's name as a witness
key_terms.صَادِقِينَ: Truthful ones — even truthful oaths are discouraged as they trivialize God's name
key_terms.كَاذِبِينَ: Liars/as liars — swearing to falsehood, which was already prohibited by Mosaic law
key_terms.مُعَلِّمَ الْخَيْرِ: Teacher of goodness — an honorific title for Prophet Isa, reflecting his role as a moral guide

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Isa (Jesus) teach about swearing oaths by God's name?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a teaching of Prophet Isa (Jesus, peace be upon him) to his disciples (hawariyyun) on the ethics of oath-taking. Citing Moses's prohibition on false oaths, Isa takes the prohibition a step further, forbidding even truthful oaths by God's name. This reflects the Islamic principle of preserving the sanctity of divine names and discouraging casual invocation of God's name in speech.
